prompt_text: Who is the best orthodontist in Houston for braces or Invisalign?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” orthodontist for everyone — the right one depends on your location in Houston, the complexity of your case, your goals (braces vs Invisalign), budget, and personal preferences. I can help you find a great match. Meanwhile, here’s how to identify top providers and what to ask so you pick the best orthodontist for you.

How to find top orthodontists in Houston
- Use reputable directories:
  - American Association of Orthodontists (AAO) “Find an orthodontist”
  - Invisalign “Find a doctor” locator (shows providers’ experience level)
  - Google Maps, Healthgrades, Yelp — read recent reviews and before/after photos
- Confirm they are an orthodontist (specialist), not a general dentist offering orthodontics.
- Look for American Board of Orthodontics (ABO) certification — a strong credential.
- Check provider Invisalign status (Gold, Platinum, Diamond) if considering Invisalign; higher tiers usually indicate more experience with many cases.
- View before/after galleries and patient testimonials for similar cases (teen vs adult, complex bite issues).

Questions to ask at the consult
- Are you a board-certified orthodontist? How long have you done braces/Invisalign?
- Which systems do you use (traditional braces, clear braces, Invisalign, clear aligners from other companies)?
- How many Invisalign/case-types like mine have you treated?
- Do you offer digital scans (iTero/3D) and show predicted outcomes?
- Estimated treatment time, total cost, payment options and insurance/FSA use
- Who handles emergencies and after-hours issues? What’s included (retainers, lost tray policy)?
- Will I need extractions, surgery, or other specialists involved?
- Can I see before/after photos or talk to current/recent patients?

Clinical tips: braces vs Invisalign
- Invisalign works well for many adult and teen cases; it may be less ideal for some severe bite or jaw movement cases. Ask whether your case is predictable with aligners.
- Experienced orthodontists often use both braces and Invisalign; the best choice is the one recommended for your specific problem, not just the newest technology.
- Look for practices that use digital planning and present a clear treatment plan.

Practical next step
If you tell me your Houston neighborhood or zip code (and whether this is for a child or adult and whether you prefer Invisalign or braces), I can pull up several highly rated nearby orthodontic practices and suggest 3–5 to call for consults and compare.
